text:
matt: heads up — we've got a blast of GPU attach failures in us-west1 starting ~03:10 UTC. lots of 'attach stuck' and provisioning timeouts. looks correlated with local NVMe iops spikes.
anika: seeing the same. scrubber/janitor concurrency jumped around 03:11. lots of deep-scrub tasks started simultaneously.
storage-bot: ALERT: io-util > 95% on /dev/nvme0n1 across 62 hosts in us-west1 (window 03:10-03:16 UTC). provisioning-failures spike +18%.
ops-oncall: did anyone roll a janitor tuning last night? we had a canary for janitor-v2 at 02:50 but it shouldn't expand until 04:00.
dave: that was me — rolled a config change to increase janitor parallelism for faster cleanup. thought we scoped to cold pool only, but looks like scope rule misfire. investigating now. sorry.
matt: ok immediate mitigation: 1) reduce janitor concurrency for ephemeral pool to 2 2) pause deep-scrub on nodes with 'gpu-critical' tag 3) temporarily bias provisioning away from us-west1 if capacity exists elsewhere. cost > more delayed cleanup but unblocks customers.
anika: running command: `janitorctl set-concurrency --pool=ephemeral --concurrency=2 --reason="emergency iops"`
storage-bot: ACTION: janitor concurrency lowered to 2 for ephemeral pool (applied to 1,143 hosts).
sanjay: created tracking ticket STOR-6789: "ephemeral janitor scope misfire -> iops surge -> gpu attach failures". assigning to dave + infra-storage.
ops-oncall: pausing deep-scrub on gpu-critical tag now: `janitorctl pause-scrub --tag=gpu-critical` -> applied.
storage-bot: PAUSE: deep-scrub paused on 370 gpu-critical hosts.
dave: rollback of the rollout is in progress for the canary rule. root cause: scope rule used wrong label selector; fix will be in next patch.
matt: after lowering concurrency attach success rate improved: 78% -> 96% in 12m. iops on affected devices dropped from 95% util to ~48%. here's a quick iostat snippet from host gnode-514: 

Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  await  r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1         320.2  1040.6  4096.0 16384.0  12.3   1.9    13.5   0.45  49.7

anika: good recovery. follow-up action items: - add pre-check to janitor scheduler to skip nodes with pending gpu-allocs - add soft quota so scrub can't exceed 20% io per device - schedule deep-scrub to midnight-only by default for gpu pools
sanjay: will scope the scheduler pre-check in STOR-6789 and add alert rules: local-io-util > 85% + provisioning-failures > 3% -> pager.
ops-oncall: documenting emergency steps in runbook and adding playbook snippet for 'janitor concurrency throttle'.
dave: will push fix for the selector bug today and add a canary gate to prevent global expansion until manual check.
matt: thumbs up. please add a cost note: delaying cleanup increases storage retention (S3/ephemeral GC window) and may bump reserved capacity needs for a few hours — tradeoff ok for availability. :thumbsup:
anika: also suggest a follow-up perf test: simulate scrub at 2x concurrency on a subset of devices to quantify safe thresholds.
sanjay: noted in STOR-6789. tagging infra-scheduling and eng-sre.
storage-bot: METRIC: attach-success-rate(us-west1) recovered to 96% at 03:23 UTC. ongoing monitoring enabled.
ops-oncall: closing incident channel once postmortem draft is up. can someone grab a short postmortem?
dave: i'll draft root-cause + remediation plan and share. thanks everyone for the quick responses.
matt: great coordination — reassigning follow-ups to infra-storage. :white_check_mark:
